blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, the month-end close is not a routine — it is a discipline that determines how fast the leadership team can make decisions. A company that closes its books by the third working day of the following month can act on real numbers before its competitors have even looked at theirs. A company that closes on the fifteenth is always reacting to last month's reality while this month is already halfway over.

Fast close is not achieved by rushing. It is achieved by design: clean sub-ledgers all month, automated reconciliations where possible, documented estimates for the few items that cannot be final by day one, and a short, rehearsed checklist for the final hours of close.

Rarely does a slow close reflect a careless team. More often, it reflects an organisation that never decided to invest in close discipline — and quietly lost the strategic advantage that fast, trusted numbers give every month.

items.q: According to the text, what does the month-end close ultimately determine?
options: How fast the leadership team can make decisions
How large the finance team needs to be
How many sub-ledgers a company keeps
How much the audit will cost
items.why: "a discipline that determines how fast the leadership team can make decisions."

items.q: How is a fast close achieved, according to the text?
options: By design — clean sub-ledgers, automated reconciliations and a rehearsed checklist
By hiring more accountants at month-end
By postponing difficult items to the next quarter
By rushing the final hours of the month
items.why: "Fast close is not achieved by rushing. It is achieved by design…"

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Some items can be booked as documented estimates rather than final figures.
Close discipline is built through the whole month, not just at the end.
A slow close is usually the sign of a lazy, careless team.
Trusted numbers delivered early create a competitive advantage.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "Rarely does a slow close reflect a careless team" — a causa é falta de investimento, não descuido.

items.q: What does the contrast between closing "by the third working day" and "on the fifteenth" suggest?
options: Speed of close translates directly into decision-making advantage
The exact date of close is a purely administrative detail
Larger companies always close later than smaller ones
Both timelines are equally acceptable in practice
items.why: Inferência: quem fecha cedo age sobre números reais antes dos concorrentes; quem fecha tarde vive reagindo.

items.q: What does "quietly lost the strategic advantage" imply about the cost of a slow close?
options: The loss is dramatic and immediately visible on the P&L
There is no real cost, only a perception problem
The loss is invisible month to month, yet real and recurring
The cost falls entirely on the external auditors
items.why: Inferência: "quietly" indica uma perda silenciosa — não aparece de repente, mas se repete todo mês.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando o programa de fechamento à liderança de finanças. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Let me be blunt about where we stand. Right now it takes us twelve working days to close, and by the time the numbers land, the board has already made half its decisions on gut feel. That is the problem I have been asked to fix.

My target is four working days by the end of the programme. And let me stop the obvious objection here: not once will we get there by asking anyone to work faster in the final week. Speed at the end is a symptom, not a cure.

So we are designing the whole thing a year in advance. Sub-ledgers reconciled continuously, not in a panic on day one. Automated reconciliations wherever the volume justifies it. And for the handful of items that genuinely cannot be final by day one, a documented estimate, agreed in advance, that nobody has to argue about at eleven at night.

What I am really selling you is not a faster close. It is trusted numbers, early enough to act on. Rarely does a finance team get the chance to hand the business a strategic advantage that costs almost nothing to keep. This is that chance — so I would ask you to back the design work before you judge the deadline.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How long does the close currently take, and what is Emily's target?
options: Twelve working days now; a target of four
Four working days now; a target of one
Ten working days now; a target of two
Fifteen days now; a target of eight
items.why: "it takes us twelve working days to close… My target is four working days."

items.q: What does Emily say about working faster in the final week?
options: It is exactly what she wants the team to do
It only matters for the smallest sub-ledgers
It is the main way they will hit the target
It is not how they will get there — speed at the end is a symptom, not a cure
items.why: "not once will we get there by asking anyone to work faster… Speed at the end is a symptom, not a cure."

items.q: How does Emily plan to handle items that cannot be final by day one?
options: Leave them out of the close entirely
Push them into the following quarter
Use a documented estimate agreed in advance
Reconcile them manually at eleven at night
items.why: "a documented estimate, agreed in advance, that nobody has to argue about at eleven at night."

items.q: When Emily says the board "has already made half its decisions on gut feel," she is implying that…
options: the numbers themselves are inaccurate
the board prefers intuition to data
the board does not read finance reports at all
the current close is too slow to inform real decisions in time
items.why: Inferência: os números chegam tarde demais, então a decisão já foi tomada sem eles.

items.q: What is Emily really asking the leadership to commit to?
options: Backing the design work rather than reacting to the deadline
Hiring more staff for the final week of close
Abandoning automated reconciliations to save cost
Judging the deadline before any design work begins
items.why: Inferência: "back the design work before you judge the deadline" — ela pede confiança no método, não no prazo isolado.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We reconcile the intercompany balances every working day, not just at month-end." A working day is…
options: a day when overtime is paid
a business day, excluding weekends and holidays
any day the market is open
the last day of the accounting period
items.why: Working day = dia útil: exclui fins de semana e feriados.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The cash figure was wrong because the ___ had not been reconciled against the bank."
options: checklist
sub-ledger
strategic advantage
trial balance
items.why: Sub-ledger = livro auxiliar, que alimenta o razão principal e precisa bater com o banco.

items.q: "For accruals we book a documented estimate and true it up next month." An estimate is…
options: a final, audited figure
a formal approval from the CFO
a reconciliation of two ledgers
an approximate value used before the exact number is known
items.why: Estimate = estimativa: um valor aproximado usado até se ter o número exato.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Nobody scrambled at midnight; the team simply worked through a short, ___ checklist."
options: automated
trusted
careless
rehearsed
items.why: Rehearsed checklist = checklist ensaiado, praticado de antemão para não haver improviso.

items.q: "Delivering the numbers on day four gave us a real strategic advantage." This means…
options: a temporary accounting adjustment
an edge over competitors that helps the business win
a purely internal reporting benefit with no external value
a reduction in the audit fee
items.why: Strategic advantage = vantagem estratégica: uma dianteira que ajuda o negócio a competir e vencer.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de fechamento e projetos financeiros. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The controller still has to sign off on the final trial balance." To sign off on means to…
options: delay until next month
quietly revise
formally approve
circulate for comment
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new close calendar to each entity next quarter." To roll out means to…
options: implement in stages
audit in secret
explain to the auditors
cancel gradually
items.why: Roll out = implantar de forma progressiva, entidade por entidade.

items.q: "Two regional controllers pushed back on the four-day target." They…
options: approved it at once
resisted or challenged it
forgot to respond
rewrote the whole calendar
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed the new checklist but never followed through." They…
options: handed it to the auditors
changed it every month
failed to carry it out to completion
documented it in detail
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Shaving one day off the close won't move the needle unless the sub-ledgers are clean." This means it will…
options: take too long to measure
trigger an audit finding
cost far more than expected
not make a meaningful difference
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível, mexer o ponteiro de fato.
